private_note: One draw, no second chance, so I weigh the downside heavily but won't throw away the mean. Alder keeps the average at 100, raises my floor from 22 to 32, and guarantees health coverage; it beats Today in every way I care about. Cedar's higher mean comes with a 1-in-5 chance of 15 and no coverage. Birch and Hazel cut the average about 20 percent. Hazel's floor is best, but by a log-utility check Today edges it.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will land in, and we each get one draw that lasts a generation. I propose Alder. It keeps the average household at 100, the same as today, so the economy we will live in is no smaller. But it lifts the bottom from 22 to 32 and guarantees everyone basic health coverage. That matters most to whichever of us draws the lowest fifth, and any of us might. The top fifth gives up only about 4 percent. Cedar raises the average, but it bets one in five of us on 15 and no health coverage. Birch and Hazel protect the bottom, but they shrink everyone's average income by about a fifth. Alder is the insurance policy each of us would buy for ourselves. We need nine votes, and failure leaves us with today. Alder beats today for every delegate who fears the bottom and costs little to those who hope for the top.
